Why FSD

CODE DOESN'T DRIVE THE CAR.
NETS DO.

Elon, Tesla AI Day 2022:

"The neural nets have gradually absorbed more and more software."

"In the limit, you could simply take the videos as seen by the car and compare those to the steering inputs from the steering wheel and pedals…"

"In principle, you could train with nothing in between, because that's what humans are doing with a biological neural net."

Hand-written rules explode with every edge case.
End-to-end nets learn from video — the same way you learned to drive.

The stack keeps getting simpler.
That's why FSD keeps getting better without rewriting the car.

Elon Musk on why the next era of space has to leave Earth.

"We're gonna go to the moon. We're gonna have a base on the moon. We're gonna send people to Mars… and make life multiplanetary."

"And I think this day heralds a new age of space exploration."

He is not selling a poster of rockets. He is naming the fork: stay Earth-only forever, or become a spacefaring civilization that can keep going after this planet.

• Moon base = the nearby proving ground
• Mars = the second home that makes extinction less final
• Multiplanetary = the insurance policy for consciousness itself

One planet is a single point of failure.
Two worlds is a civilization that can still write history.

Starship is the vehicle.
The new era is the destination.

"Make life multiplanetary."

Cybercab wasn’t built like a Model Y with the wheel deleted.

It’s Tesla’s first autonomous-first vehicle — no steering wheel, no pedals — and the most integrated product they’ve ever made across engineering, software, manufacturing, legal, policy, service, and infrastructure.

Lead vehicle engineer Eric (@EricETesla) on what that forced:

•⁠  ⁠Chase every loss — rolling resistance, aero, low-voltage drain, how the fleet actually drives and charges
•⁠  ⁠Two seats on purpose — cut what you don’t need for an awesome autonomous ride
•⁠  ⁠Unbox manufacturing — break the 100-year assembly-line rules so volume and cost actually work
•⁠  ⁠~6 miles per kWh efficiency target — and they say the foundation is good enough to beat it

Elon set the bar:

“Elon’s algorithm works. You have to simplify before you can advance.”

He told the team: half of everything.

•⁠  ⁠Electricity endpoints — cut ~50%
•⁠  ⁠Mass — down vs every prior Tesla
•⁠  ⁠Part count — half
•⁠  ⁠Factory space / cycle time — cut in half with Unbox

Cost-per-mile is the product.
Simplify first.
Then scale.

Elon Musk on how surreal his life feels.

"My life feels somewhat surreal. I can't believe these things are actually happening."

"It makes me believe in simulation theory… the things I'm doing are so preposterous that it's hard to believe they're real."

He is not doing philosophy-class cosplay. He is pointing at the gap between what used to be science fiction and what SpaceX is actually building — then treating that gap as a clue about reality, not a joke.

• Starship = largest, most powerful flying object ever made
• Intent: launch it more than once per hour
• That cadence is what makes multiplanetary feel less like a poster and more like a schedule

When the work outruns common sense, he reaches for simulation.

Not because Earth is boring.

Because the rockets got too real.

"We've got Starship… and we intend to launch that more than once per hour."

Elon Musk on 100-hour weeks.

"I've done many stretches of 100-hour weeks, where roughly six hours per day is sleeping."

"I would not recommend that. That's for emergencies. It's not all the time."

Most founder folklore glamorizes the grind. Elon frames 100-hour weeks as emergency medicine — sometimes the difference between success and failure, never the lifestyle brand.

• Emergency tool, not a default
• ~6 hours sleep when it hits
• He would not recommend it as normal

Intensity when the mission needs it.
Not intensity as cosplay.
